correctness.rationale: For A=π(kn), B=π((k+1)n), the real-root inequality and the strict integer-power inequality are equivalent because both counts are positive. For n≥300, the Brun–Titchmarsh interval estimate with start kn and length n, and the Rosser–Schoenfeld lower bound at kn, apply within their stated ranges. They give k log(B/A)≤k(B−A)/A<2 log(kn)/log n≤4, where kn≤n²; if B=A the strict upper bound is immediate. Meanwhile log A≥log 62>4, using the elementary exponential series bound e<11/4 and (11/4)^4<62. The independent segmented-sieve exact replay covers every n=5,…,299 and k=1,…,n, confirming all 44,840 inequalities, π(300)=62, and minimum positive margin 4 at (n,k)=(6,1). The threshold and finite range join without a gap.
residual_risks: The classical analytic inequalities are inputs, not reproved by the certificate. The original Montgomery–Vaughan full text and exact Rosser–Schoenfeld passage were not retrieved on the attempted lawful routes. Finite arithmetic does not certify the analytic tail.
